name: Crystal Palace Subway
description: A vaulted polychrome-brick subway (1865) that once led from the old railway station to the Crystal Palace — a surviving Victorian treasure below the High Level station.
tips: Free — open on select heritage days only, including Open House London. Breathtaking.

name: Severndroog Castle
description: A Gothic triangular folly (1784) atop Shooter's Hill — on a clear day you can see 7 counties from the roof.
tips: Open first Sunday of the month plus heritage days. £2 climb. Woolwich is nearest station.

name: Canonbury Tower
description: A 16th-century brick tower in Canonbury Square — once home to Sir Francis Bacon and Oliver Goldsmith, now an occasionally opened historic venue.
tips: Open House London weekend only, or by arrangement. Free to visit Canonbury Square gardens.

name: Crossness Engines
description: The gorgeous 'Cathedral on the Marsh' — Bazalgette's 1865 sewage pumping station, spectacular painted Victorian ironwork, with 'steaming days' running four times a year.
tips: Steaming days (engines running) are special — book well ahead.

name: Little Angel Theatre
description: London's specialist puppet theatre in Islington — runs its own puppet-making and shows for children and adults since 1961.
tips: Perfect for children 3+. Some shows are adult-only.

name: Unicorn Theatre
description: A dedicated young audiences' theatre near London Bridge — adventurous, commissioning new plays from the best UK writers.
tips: Two stages — choose by age range. Family audio-described performances available.

name: Polka Theatre
description: Wimbledon children's theatre — one of Britain's only theatres exclusively for kids under 12, recently redesigned and glorious.
tips: New building opened 2022. Café and playroom excellent.

name: Mahogany Bar at Wilton's Music Hall
description: The attached bar of Wilton's Music Hall — operating in the same 1858 building as the theatre, perfect for a gig-free visit.
tips: Free to enter. Open Mon-Fri + some weekends. A time-machine feeling.

name: Watts Memorial, Postman's Park
description: GF Watts's 1900 memorial to 'heroic self-sacrifice' — hand-painted Doulton tiles commemorating ordinary Londoners who died saving others.
tips: Free. Read every tile — each tells a heartbreaking story.

name: The London Seance
description: Immersive themed dining experiences from companies like Swamp Motel and ABBA Voyage at Lewisham — bookable immersive entertainment where you are part of the show.
tips: Multiple operators — Punchdrunk, Secret Cinema, Swamp Motel etc. Check current shows.
